---

## What Is ROR?

[ROR](https://ror.org) (the Research Organization Registry) is a global, community-led registry of open persistent identifiers for research organizations. Every organization in the registry is assigned a **ROR ID** — a URL of the form `https://ror.org/xxxxxxxxx` — that refers to that organization and nothing else. ROR is operated as a collaborative initiative by the California Digital Library, Crossref, and DataCite, and it is committed to the [Principles of Open Scholarly Infrastructure](https://openscholarlyinfrastructure.org). All ROR data is available under [CC0 1.0](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) via a free REST API and a public data dump.

ROR serves the same purpose for organizations that [ORCID](https://orcid.org) iDs serve for people and DOIs serve for research outputs. Crucially, it is the default identifier supported in **Crossref DOI metadata**, **DataCite DOI metadata**, and **ORCID records**, so it is the natural way to record an affiliation across most of the scholarly infrastructure we interact with.

### What it is for

Organizations change their names, merge, and move to new web addresses, which makes it hard to reliably connect an institution to its outputs. A ROR ID stays fixed while all of that changes. Use it to:

- Disambiguate our organization from others with similar names — there are many "Open Science Centers".
- Link our tutorials, software, datasets, and publications back to us as an organization.
- Keep affiliations meaningful across our own renaming: our domain moved from `uni-muenchen.de` to `lmu.de`, and our name appears in several variations in the wild (see below).

The main thing to avoid is supplying our affiliation only as free text. Wherever a system offers a ROR ID field, use it.

## Our ROR Record

Our record is **<https://ror.org/029e6qe04>**, and it is in `active` status.

"LMU Open Science Center" is the registry's **display name** for us, i.e. the preferred label. The other names listed are recognized aliases and acronyms, so a search for any of them should surface our record. Where a system has both a name field and a ROR ID field, entering our display name plus the ROR ID is the most useful combination.

::: {.callout-note}
#### Ours or LMU München's?

We are an organizational unit of LMU München, so our record is a child of the [LMU München record](https://ror.org/05591te55). Use **our** ROR ID when the Open Science Center itself is the responsible organization — for our tutorials, our software, and our own events. Use the **LMU München** ROR ID when the relevant organization is the university as a whole. 
:::

## Open Items

### Website link is out of date

The record still points to `https://www.osc.uni-muenchen.de`, but our site now lives at <https://www.osc.lmu.de>. We opened an update request in June 2026:

- [ror-updates issue #35540](https://github.com/ror-community/ror-updates/issues/35540) — modify the organization website to `https://www.osc.lmu.de/`. Opened 10 June 2026; still open as of September 2026.


### ROR is not yet usable in CITATION.cff

There is no way to record our ROR ID in a `CITATION.cff` file today. As of September 2026 the current released version of the Citation File Format, **CFF 1.2.0** (released August 2021), has no `ror` field for entities — confirmed against the [1.2.0 schema](https://github.com/citation-file-format/citation-file-format/blob/1.2.0/schema.json).

The capability has been merged into CFF's `develop` branch, and ROR documents [how to add ROR iDs to CFF](https://ror.readme.io/v2/docs/add-ror-ids-to-cff), but it will only be released with **CFF 1.3.0**. The maintainers have said they cannot estimate a release date due to restricted resources, and the [1.3.0 milestone](https://github.com/citation-file-format/citation-file-format/milestone/8) remains open. Relevant discussions: [issue #484](https://github.com/citation-file-format/citation-file-format/issues/484) (add a `ror` key for entities) and [issue #548](https://github.com/citation-file-format/citation-file-format/issues/548) (document that `ror` iDs will be supported).

If CFF 1.3.0 lands, our [CITATION.cff](../CITATION.cff) is a candidate for an update so that the OSC can be credited as an organizational author with a machine-readable identifier rather than a plain name string. Until then there is nothing to add.

If a change to our record is ever needed, submit it through the [ROR curation request form](https://curation-request.ror.org) or as an issue in the [ror-updates repository](https://github.com/ror-community/ror-updates). Requests are reviewed by ROR's curation team, so expect a wait.
